title: Consolidated SDK Adapter + Enterprise Patterns Intake
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Collect and triage a batch of customer requests asking for a more consistent SDK surface that solves three recurrent pain points: (1) language parity for new clients (Go, Rust, C#), (2) enterprise auth patterns (token rotation, SSO/OIDC, delegated credentials, KMS hooks), and (3) streaming ergonomics (backpressure handling, resumable streams, standardized event framing). This ticket is the PM intake + prioritization artifact that will feed scoped work for ENG/design and produce a set of accepted RFCs or sub-tickets.
background: Over the past 6 months we've received ~18 customer asks and multiple AE signals from Enterprise accounts asking for predictable auth flows (SSO + long-lived service principals), and several OSS consumers reporting inconsistent streaming behavior across languages. Current SDKs have per-language divergences in reconnect/backpressure semantics and ad-hoc auth helpers. This creates friction for platform teams embedding Redwood API into backend services that must meet security/compliance controls.
acceptance_criteria: A documented triage outcome that groups requests into: language gaps, auth patterns, streaming ergonomics, and low-effort UX fixes
A prioritized backlog of sub-issues (PM/ENG/DES) with estimates and owners
Defined proposal for a "unified client adapter" pattern describing responsibilities, wire format and minimal runtime contracts
Security sign-off criteria for enterprise auth flows (token rotation, session revocation) documented and sent to security for review
Prototype plan for 1 language (Go) implementing the adapter + streaming contract, with test harness and perf goals
decisions: Adapter pattern: prefer thin, language-specific shims that call a shared core runtime contract rather than shipping a single binary across languages (decision 2026-03-04, ENG consensus)
Streaming framing: standardize on newline-delimited JSON events with separate 'control' envelope for flow-control tokens (proposal accepted 2026-03-06)
Auth approach: support both short-lived bearer tokens + automatic refresh hooks; add standard OIDC client flow in SDKs and a pluggable credential provider interface (security asked for formal review)
Rollout: pilot Go adapter in an early access program, collect telemetry, then iterate on Rust and C# based on signal
updates: 2026-02-28 Aisha Patel - Ticket created following consolidated AE intake spreadsheet (link in 'links'). Initial scope proposed to focus on adapter pattern + Go pilot.

2026-03-02 Miguel Santos - Met with runtime eng team; ENG flagged two blockers: kvcache API gaps for resumable streams, and kernel scheduling impacts for persistent connections. Added ENG-2048 and ENG-2075 as dependencies.

2026-03-04 Devon Lee (ENG) - Engineering review: recommended thin shim approach to avoid cross-language binary distribution. Noted measurable cost of maintaining identical high-level APIs across languages.

2026-03-06 Laura Kim (Design) - UX review: recommended a simple streaming consumer API that exposes a buffered iterator and an explicit pause/resume primitive; asked to mock three flows for sidebar review.
2026-03-09 Aisha Patel - Prioritization workshop with solutions and sales; prioritized enterprise auth (token rotation, session revocation) and Go streaming adapter as P1; Rust and C# as P2.

2026-03-12 Miguel Santos - Drafted RFC for unified client adapter and uploaded prototype plan. Security review requested and assigned to Priya Nair (security). Added prototype milestone to cycle 2026-W12.
risks: Cross-language maintenance cost if parity is enforced strictly
Potential security review delays around delegated credential patterns
Runtime performance regressions if streaming abstraction forces synchronous processing paths
review_feedback: Security (Priya Nair): require threat model for token refresh flows and revocation before GA
Design (Laura Kim): provide 3 concrete UX patterns: push-consumer, pull-iterator, and event-callback; prefer pull-iterator for server-side SDKs
Solutions (Jordan Meyers): ask for migration guide, sample infra config for token rotation with HashiCorp Vault and AWS KMS
next_steps: Finalize RFC and attach acceptance criteria (due 2026-03-19)
Kick off Go pilot ticket ENG-2176 (create sub-issue) and allocate 2-sprint effort
Security to run threat model on proposed credential provider interface (Priya assigned)
Design to deliver API mocks and 3 flow diagrams by 2026-03-22
Add telemetry events to track reconnect rate, dropped frames, and auth refresh errors in pilot
